record: Tunisian National Heritage Institute archaeological site inventory
facts: The theatre dates to AD 168 or 169, seats roughly 3,500 and was restored in 1908 and 1911. It has a three-part cavea and re-erected stage columns.

record: Université Côte d’Azur historical photographic collection catalogue measurements
facts: Records the 63.5 metre cavea span, 15 metre elevation change, groups of 9, 6 and 4 main rows, five lower rows for dignitaries, and stage measuring 36.75 by 5.5 metres.
Locates the standing theatre in the northeastern part of the protected Dougga archaeological site.
